final.reason: Six full-transient evaluations were used. Key findings: (1) The direct branch's clamp (3.3 V) minus 2 diode drops minus the 5000 Ω series drop makes storage asymptote near ~3.0 V, so the original gate 2.9 V is at the edge and the MCU is very hard to start. (2) The main beam at the nominal 35 mm resonates ~35 Hz, detuned from the 45 Hz background; the switched/rectified harvester is strongly electrically damped, so charging from 0.15 g is weak. (3) Digital confirmation math is sound: a 210 Hz target in 128 pts @2048 Hz yields band fraction ~0.8–0.89 with RMS > 0.12 g, while 250 Hz nuisance gives ~0.01, so confirmation/rejection is not the blocker. Experimentally, every combination tried (main 29.5–35 mm, aux 18–21.4 mm, C 80–330 µF, gate 2.0–2.9 V, threshold 0.15–0.55 V) returned exactly faults=4, delivered_on_time=0, false_reports=0, with only the mechanical safety slacks changing (stress depends only on aux length, travel only on main length; both <1). This invariance indicates the service failure is governed by a fixed, unresolved effective-length (manufacturing/mounting) factor that detunes the narrow-band beams, which the pass/fail-plus-slack feedback did not let me identify to the required ~1–2% precision. I could not find a passing design, but a failed search is not a proof over the whole legal space, so INFEASIBLE is not justified. Status UNKNOWN; final evaluated design is main=34.0 mm, aux=20.8 mm, C=100 µF, gate=2.0 V, threshold=0.15 V (feasibility unconfirmed).
